subject: Chemistry
title: Halogen Exchange: Finkelstein and Swarts Reactions
summary: Halogen exchange (NCERT 6.4.3) swaps the Cl or Br of an alkyl halide for another halogen. Finkelstein: R–X + NaI in dry acetone gives R–I; NaCl / NaBr is insoluble in dry acetone and precipitates, so by Le Chatelier's principle the reaction goes forward. Swarts: heating R–Cl / R–Br with a heavy metallic fluoride (AgF, Hg₂F₂, CoF₂ or SbF₃) gives the alkyl fluoride. Trick: Finkelstein → iodide, Swarts → fluoride.

notes.title: Finkelstein and Swarts Reactions
notes.blurb: both reactions, why Finkelstein goes forward, the four Swarts reagents, a side-by-side table and common mistakes

keyPoints: **Finkelstein:** R–X + NaI → R–I + NaX (X = Cl, Br), in **dry acetone**: makes alkyl iodides.
NaCl / NaBr is **insoluble in dry acetone** and precipitates; by **Le Chatelier's principle** the reaction moves forward.
**Swarts:** heat R–Cl / R–Br with a metallic fluoride, **AgF, Hg₂F₂, CoF₂ or SbF₃**: makes alkyl fluorides.
Direct fluorination with F₂ is violent, so alkyl fluorides are made by the Swarts reaction.

blocks.p: **R–X + NaI → R–I + NaX** (X = Cl, Br), with **dry acetone** written over the arrow. Iodide replaces chloride or bromide on the carbon. NaI dissolves in dry acetone but **NaCl and NaBr do not**: they precipitate, a product leaves the solution, and by **Le Chatelier's principle** the equilibrium shifts forward, giving a good yield of alkyl iodide.
Examples: CH₃CH₂Cl + NaI → CH₃CH₂I + NaCl↓ (chloroethane → iodoethane); CH₃Br + NaI → CH₃I + NaBr↓ (bromomethane → iodomethane).

Heating an alkyl chloride or bromide with a **heavy metallic fluoride** (AgF, Hg₂F₂, CoF₂ or SbF₃) gives the **alkyl fluoride**. Direct fluorination with F₂ is violent, so this is the best laboratory route.
Examples: H₃C–Br + AgF → H₃C–F + AgBr (on heating); 2 CH₃CH₂Cl + Hg₂F₂ → 2 CH₃CH₂F + Hg₂Cl₂.
